comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: If this file is automatically generated, should we `.gitignore` it?
comments.label_reasoning: The comment questions whether an auto-generated file should be excluded from version control via .gitignore, which is a file/folder organization and project structure concern.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment asks whether the file should be added to .gitignore, implying a concrete change to the repository's ignore rules.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
It would be super cool to see this sponsor code working too :)

I'd recommend deleting commented out code though if it's a WIP. You can always browse the git history if you want to see it again.
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer explicitly recommends deleting commented-out code, which is a classic dead-code related issue.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment explicitly recommends deleting commented-out code, which is a concrete code change request.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: Why this over `ts-node-esm`, which we're using in the root `package.json`?
comments.label_reasoning: The comment questions the choice of runtime/tooling (not using `ts-node-esm` as used elsewhere in the project), pointing to an inconsistency with project-level conventions and standards.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
Initially copied over the code from vitest, but esno is infact faster than ts-node-esm. 
We can replace ts-node-esm with esno completely in a different PR.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Sounds good!

Btw, it looks like `esno` now just redirects to `tsx`, so we should probably use that directly instead. See https://github.com/esbuild-kit/esno/commit/01065aa6eec022616550298e7781be81bb78575c

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Replacing ts-node-esm didn't work, as some weird `__name` is not defined error was thrown during mermaid runtime (the scripts ran fine, error was only when running `dev`). So I've just used ts-node-esm everywhere.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: :+1: It sounds like this is a known limitation with `tsx`: https://github.com/esbuild-kit/tsx/issues/113#issuecomment-1274694577, apparently it can't handle `eval()`-ing code well (`esbuild` might have similar limitations).

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The question implies a suggestion to consider using `ts-node-esm` instead of the current choice, which would be a concrete change to the package configuration.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Btw, since Node.JS v10.12.0, Node's builtin `mkdir` function now supports the `recursive: true` option, that should do the same thing as `ensureDir`.

This means we should be able to remove the `fs-extra` library, and just use `node:fs/promises`!

See https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fspromisesmkdirpath-options

```suggestion
  await fs.mkdir(fileURLToPath(new URL('..', getAvatarPath('none'))), {recursive: true});
```
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer suggests removing the `fs-extra` dependency in favor of Node.js built-in `fs/promises`, reducing unnecessary third-party library usage and improving resource/dependency efficiency.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment explicitly suggests replacing `fs-extra`'s `ensureDir` with Node's built-in `fs.mkdir` with `recursive: true`, and even provides a code suggestion implementing the change.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: This isn't something for you to do in this PR, but what do you think about the `packages/mermaid/src/docs` folder into something like `packages/docs`? It might make it easier to split out what `devDependencies` we have for `mermaid`, and what `devDependencies` we only need for the docs.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: Thanks for making an issue, (link at https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/issues/4382, in case anyone is looking at this PR from the future)!
